originalTitle: Ordered dyadic cycle completion controls crossings
originalHypotheses: One fixed matching of positive and negative dated tokens.
Locally finite dates and matched endpoint ratio at most a constant κ≥1.
independence: Proof reconstructed from primary arguments and explicit definitions. Earlier source status/review assertions were not treated as proof. The author previously collected these sources; the present derivations and finite/exact-algebra checks are new independent audit work.
detailedDerivation: Bucket each matched pair by k=floor(log2 minimum date). Endpoint ratioκ places the entire pair in [2^k,2κ2^k), so each bucket is finite.
At cut n, x_i=1[P_i≤n] is nonincreasing under the specified positive-date sorting, while z_i=1[M_i≤n]. For a cyclic bucket, triangle inequality gives Σ|x_i−z_(i+1)|≤Σ|x_i−x_(i+1)|+Σ|x_(i+1)−z_(i+1)|.
The last sum is the bucket’s original matching crossings. The cyclic x transition count is0 if constant and2 otherwise. Every nonconstant bucket has 2^k≤n and2κ2^k>n.

The half-open scale interval n/(2κ)<2^k≤n has at most ceil(log2(2κ)) powers of2. Adding original and added crossings yields W_G≤2W_M+2ceil(log2(2κ)). Singleton buckets add nothing; tied positive dates do not change monotonicity.
For κ=4 the correction is6. This bound requires the chosen order; it does not hold by this argument for arbitrary bucket permutations.
